correctness.rationale: For each coordinate \(i\), independent row choices induce a Bernoulli variable with parameter \(p_i\) and an augmented pair of exactly specified update matrices. The explicitly constructed strictly positive-definite \(W=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&t\\t&1\end{psmallmatrix}\) satisfies \(\mathcal L(W)=W-dE_{11}\) and \(\mathcal L^2(W)=W-d\begin{psmallmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{psmallmatrix}\); the final displayed matrix is positive definite. Positivity proves geometric convergence when \(d>0\). At \(d=0\), \(W\) is fixed; for \(d<0\), \(W\) expands in positive-semidefinite order. Decomposition of \(W\) into two rank-one deterministic initial covariances gives genuine nondecay/divergence deterministic witnesses. Since \(\operatorname{sign}(d)=\operatorname{sign}(2-\alpha-\alpha^2p_i)\), summation over coordinates yields the exact global iff condition. The maximum sampling probability is at least \(1/m\), which yields the sharp dimension law; the first-moment polynomial \(z^2-z+\alpha p\) and exact fraction calculations establish the remaining claims. Standalone exact-rational verification passed.

originality.rationale: Relevant full texts were checked for the exact one-commit-old additive update and its probability-vector necessary-and-sufficient mean-square threshold, not merely title matches. Coleman documents experimental adaptive Kaczmarz instability without the stated static-law theorem; Liu–Wright–Sridhar gives a sufficient bound for another async model; Jensen et al. treats nonuniform asynchronous implementations; the public exact Gauss–Seidel delay law uses a different overwrite operator; classic jump-system results give an implicit covariance/spectral test rather than the explicit sharp row-diversity and equal-collision distinction. This is a qualified self-review, not a claim of exhaustiveness or independent certification.

value.rationale: The unstable concentration of stale row updates is motivated by current experiments on asynchronous randomized Kaczmarz. The explicit iff threshold identifies a nontrivial parameter phase even at zero row coherence, quantifies the minimum number of independently available orthogonal rows supporting a given relaxation, and shows analytically that two sampling policies with identical global adjacent-row collision probability can have opposite mean-square behavior. In addition, the rigorously exhibited mean-vs-mean-square separation prevents an unjustified inference from expected iterate stability. These are natural structural boundaries, not an arbitrary slice or textbook renaming. The source algorithms are not claimed to obey this surrogate model in actual parallel runs.
